correctness.rationale: The proof solves all three positive per-capita equilibrium equations, rigorously identifies the negative-strength domain through a strictly increasing scalar parameter, and computes the four-by-four Jacobian. Direct determinant expansion gives a positive-coefficient quartic. The Routh–Hurwitz determinant then classifies strict stability, instability and imaginary-pair boundaries. The nullification point has an exact factored determinant with precisely two positive simple roots. A separate standalone SymPy calculation confirms the symbolic identities, factorization and 27 finite eigenvalue examples; sample spectra are supplementary, not proof.

value.rationale: The source motivates onset speed as an ecological mechanism but primarily simulates parameter maps. The new theorem replaces the numerical stability interpretation with an exact criterion for every negative interaction strength, and gives both algebraic boundaries at the source-defined interaction-nullification state. The open-neighborhood persistence argument makes the reentrant window structural rather than a tuned isolated sample. This is a meaningful local network-stability boundary; no global ecology or cycle claims are made.
